# Codex verification brief — structured answers (commit aa5655a)

You are an independent reviewer. Do NOT edit any tracked file. Write scratch files only under
`audit_evidence_claims/s1/`. End with exactly one line: `VERDICT: APPROVE` or `VERDICT: CHANGES REQUIRED`.

## Context

Six rounds of review of a free-prose claim checker (`src/claims.py`; reports in `audit_evidence_claims/`)
never converged, so the design changed. With a language model, the model no longer writes the answer: it
returns `{"claims": [...]}` where each claim is a fixed-kind JSON object citing an evidence edge id.
`src/structured.py` (`Verifier`, `render`) checks each claim exactly against the SQLite graph and the
program writes the answer from accepted claims only, using graph labels and values. `src/query.py`
(`answer` with `use_llm=True`, `_llm_claims`, `verify_structured`) wires it in; `src/app.py`
(`/api/structured`) and `web/try.html` box 3 expose it. `claims.py` stays as an auxiliary screen (box 4)
and is documented as fallible (README known defect 13) — it is not under review here.
Tests: `python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` (300); `tests/test_structured.py` covers this.

## The guarantee claimed (module docstring, README "Asking it things", dashboard section 06)

An accepted claim is supported by the graph: correct kind and exact keys (no free-text field; unknown keys
reject), cited edge among those retrieved for the question and live, relation and both endpoints equal to
the named entities (names must resolve, whole, to exactly those node ids), and every value equal to what the
graph stores (action type, sponsor trial count, trial phase set and status, drug max stage, trials in graph).
The rendered answer contains nothing typed by the model. It does NOT claim the chosen claims answer the
question well or completely.

## What to verify (reproduce everything; cite file:line and exact inputs)

A. **False acceptance.** Any claim the graph does not support that is accepted, on the demo questions in
   `src/query.py:main` or any other question. Try: name resolution (aliases, salts vs parents, ambiguous
   names, companies with several ids via `also_matching_ids`, parent/subsidiary, case/whitespace/Unicode,
   very long names, names that link partially), id vs name mixing, evidence ids from a different question,
   PROFILE pseudo-edges, retired edges, relation/edge mismatches, value normalization in `_norm`
   (can two different stored codes normalize to the same string? e.g. phase sets, statuses, stages,
   action types like "ANTISENSE INHIBITOR" vs "INHIBITOR"), type confusion (bool/int/float/str/None/lists of
   mixed types, duplicate JSON keys, NaN/Infinity), nested or oversized payloads, more than 50 claims.
B. **Text leakage.** Any way for model-typed text to reach the rendered answer or the user-facing page
   (render uses labels from the DB; check every field and the page's display of rejected claims for HTML
   injection in `web/try.html`).
C. **Rendering faithfulness.** Does each rendered line say exactly what the accepted facts say (e.g. the
   sponsorship line, phase lists, empty phases, action wording)?
D. **The model path.** `query.answer(use_llm=True)` and `_llm_claims`: prompt, JSON extraction from the
   reply (`re.search(r"\{.*\}", raw, re.S)`), behaviour on malformed or empty replies, the checks dict.
E. **Usefulness.** Can faithful claims an LLM would produce from the evidence shown be expressed and
   accepted for each demo question (relations, trials' phase/status, sponsor counts, drug stage/count)?
   Note claim types the schema cannot express.
F. **Docs.** README "Asking it things" and item 13, README.ko, `structured.py` docstring, dashboard
   section 06 (`web/template.html`), try page box 3/4 text: do they claim more than the code does?

## Approval bar

No known way to get a claim the graph does not support accepted, or model-typed text into the answer;
faithful claims for the demo questions can be expressed and are accepted; docs do not overclaim.
Findings that are evidence-consistent or purely about completeness are NOTES.

Report: BLOCKERS, SHOULD FIX, NOTES, each with exact input and observed output. Then the verdict line.

---
name: review
description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes ??Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** ??does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** ??does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / PRD / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you ??run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point ??a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here ??not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) ??fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A PRD/spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls. Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3.
- The brief: "Report ??per file/hunk where relevant ??every place the diff violates a documented standard. Cite the standard (file + the rule). Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings ??the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes ??that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing ??**Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions ??**Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

"""Structured answers: claims checked exactly against the graph, prose written from them.

Reading free prose for unsupported claims is a pattern match over sentence shapes,
and six adversarial rounds kept finding shapes it misread (see claims.py and README
known defect 13). This module removes the problem instead of chasing it: a language
model does not write the answer, it fills in claims, and the program writes the
answer from the claims that check out.

A claim is a small JSON object of a fixed kind with fixed keys:

  {"kind": "relation", "relation": "ACTS_ON", "subject": "osimertinib",
   "object": "EGFR", "evidence": "<edge id>", "action": "INHIBITOR"}          (action optional)
  {"kind": "relation", "relation": "EVALUATES", "subject": "NCT03909334",
   "object": "osimertinib", "evidence": "<edge id>"}
  {"kind": "relation", "relation": "SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF", "subject": "AstraZeneca",
   "object": "osimertinib", "evidence": "<edge id>", "trial_count": 14}       (trial_count optional)
  {"kind": "trial", "trial": "NCT03909334", "evidence": "<edge id>",
   "phase": ["PHASE2"], "status": "ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING"}                    (phase, status optional; one needed)
  {"kind": "drug", "drug": "osimertinib", "evidence": "<edge id>",
   "max_stage": "APPROVAL", "trials_in_graph": 118}                           (one of the two needed)

A claim is accepted only when all of these hold:

  * its kind and keys are exactly as above (an unknown key rejects the claim, so no
    free text can ride along) and every value has the expected type;
  * the cited evidence id is one of the edges retrieved for this question, and that
    edge is live in the graph (or, for a drug claim, it is the drug's own profile
    record "profile:<id>" retrieved for this question);
  * the edge's relation is the claimed relation, and its two ends are the entities
    the claim names: a name is a node id, a label that belongs to exactly one node of
    that type, or a printable-ASCII alias the entity linker resolves, as a whole, to
    exactly one node; a name that could mean several nodes is refused;
  * every value equals what the graph stores: the edge's action type, the sponsor's
    trial count, the trial's phase set and status, the drug's maximum stage, and the
    number of live trials evaluating the drug.

The answer shown to the reader is written by `render` from accepted claims only, using
the graph's own labels and values, never the claim's strings. A claim that does not
check out is reported with the reason and left out of the answer.

What this does not do: it cannot tell whether the claims chosen answer the question
well, or whether something important was left out. It guarantees that what is said is
in the graph, not that everything in the graph that matters was said.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sqlite3

RELATIONS = {"ACTS_ON": ("Drug", "Target"), "EVALUATES": ("Trial", "Drug"),
             "SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF": ("Company", "Drug")}
KEYS = {
    "relation": ({"kind", "relation", "subject", "object", "evidence"},
                 {"action", "trial_count"}),
    "trial": ({"kind", "trial", "evidence"}, {"phase", "status"}),
    "drug": ({"kind", "drug", "evidence"}, {"max_stage", "trials_in_graph"}),
}
RE_NCT = re.compile(r"NCT\d{8}")


def _norm(v: str) -> str:
    """Spelling-insensitive form of a stored code: "phase 2" = "PHASE2" = "Phase-2"."""
    return re.sub(r"[\s\-_/]+", "", v.strip().upper())


def _flat(s: str) -> str:
    """Case and punctuation aside, the same characters: letters of any script count, so
    "osimertinib가 아닌" is not the same name as "osimertinib"."""
    return " ".join(re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", s.casefold()))


def _no_constant(name):
    raise ValueError(f"{name} is not a JSON number")


def _finite_float(text):
    v = float(text)
    if v != v or v in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
        raise ValueError(f"{text} is not a finite number")      # "1e309" overflows
    return v


def _safe(v, depth=0):
    """A rejected claim echoed back, with anything JSON cannot carry made a string."""
    if depth > 20:
        return "…"
    if isinstance(v, float) and (v != v or v in (float("inf"), float("-inf"))):
        return str(v)
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {str(k): _safe(x, depth + 1) for k, x in list(v.items())[:50]}
    if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
        return [_safe(x, depth + 1) for x in list(v)[:50]]
    if v is None or isinstance(v, (bool, int, float)):
        return v
    return str(v)[:500]


class Verifier:
    def __init__(self, kg):
        self.kg = kg

    # -- entity names --------------------------------------------------------- #
    def resolve(self, name, want: str) -> tuple[set[str], str | None]:
        """Node ids a name stands for, as a whole, among nodes of type `want`."""
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip() or len(name) > 120:
            return set(), "the name must be a short non-empty string"
        name = name.strip()
        row = self.kg.conn.execute("SELECT id, type FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                                   (name,)).fetchone()
        if row:
            return ({row["id"]}, None) if row["type"] == want else (
                set(), f"{name} is a {row['type'].lower()}, not a {want.lower()}")
        if want == "Trial":
            return set(), "a trial is named by its registry id (NCT followed by 8 digits)"
        # a label exactly as the graph (and so the evidence) writes it
        rows = self.kg.conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, type FROM node WHERE lower(label)=lower(?) AND retired_at IS NULL",
            (name,)).fetchall()
        if rows:
            ids = {r["id"] for r in rows if r["type"] == want}
            if len(ids) > 1:
                return set(), (f"'{name}' is the label of {len(ids)} {want.lower()} nodes; "
                               "use the id")
            if ids:
                return ids, None
            return set(), f"{name} is a {rows[0]['type'].lower()}, not a {want.lower()}"
        if not (name.isascii() and name.isprintable()):
            # the linker drops characters it cannot read, so "osimertinib是安全的" would
            # pass as osimertinib; outside the graph's own labels, names are plain ASCII
            return set(), (f"'{name}' is not written the way the graph writes names "
                           "(use the id or the name as it appears in the evidence)")
        ents = [e for e in self.kg.link_entities(name) if e.get("type") not in ("Disease",)]
        whole = len(ents) == 1 and _flat(ents[0].get("matched_text") or "") == _flat(name)
        if whole and ents[0].get("type") != want:
            return set(), f"{name} is a {ents[0]['type'].lower()}, not a {want.lower()}"
        if not whole:
            return set(), f"'{name}' does not name exactly one {want.lower()} on its own"
        e = ents[0]
        ids = {e["id"], *e.get("also_matching_ids", [])}
        if len(ids) > 1:
            # one alias for several organisations (a group and a subsidiary named after
            # it): which one the claim means cannot be read off the name
            return set(), f"'{name}' names {len(ids)} {want.lower()} nodes; use the id"
        return ids, None

    # -- one claim ------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def check(self, claim, retrieved: set[str]) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]:
        """Return (facts to render, None) or (None, reason)."""
        if not isinstance(claim, dict):
            return None, "a claim must be a JSON object"
        kind = claim.get("kind")
        if not isinstance(kind, str) or kind not in KEYS:
            return None, f"unknown kind {kind!r}; use relation, trial or drug"
        need, may = KEYS[kind]
        keys = set(claim)
        if need - keys:
            return None, f"missing {sorted(need - keys)}"
        if keys - need - may:
            return None, f"unknown keys {sorted(keys - need - may)} (no free text is accepted)"
        ev = claim["evidence"]
        if not isinstance(ev, str) or ev not in retrieved:
            return None, "the cited evidence is not among the edges retrieved for this question"
        edge = self.kg.conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM edge WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL", (ev,)).fetchone()
        if kind == "drug" and edge is None and ev.startswith("profile:"):
            edge = {"id": ev, "rel": "PROFILE", "src": ev.split(":", 1)[1], "dst": None,
                    "props": "{}"}
        if edge is None:
            return None, "the cited evidence is not a live edge of the graph"
        return getattr(self, "_" + kind)(claim, edge)

    def _relation(self, c, edge):
        rel = c["relation"]
        if not isinstance(rel, str) or rel not in RELATIONS:
            return None, f"unknown relation {rel!r}"
        if edge["rel"] != rel:
            return None, f"the cited edge is {edge['rel']}, not {rel}"
        st, ot = RELATIONS[rel]
        s_ids, why = self.resolve(c["subject"], st)
        if why:
            return None, why
        o_ids, why = self.resolve(c["object"], ot)
        if why:
            return None, why
        if edge["src"] not in s_ids or edge["dst"] not in o_ids:
            return None, "the cited edge does not join these two entities in this direction"
        props = json.loads(edge["props"] or "{}")
        facts = {"kind": "relation", "relation": rel, "edge": edge["id"],
                 "subject": edge["src"], "object": edge["dst"]}
        if "action" in c:
            if rel != "ACTS_ON" or not isinstance(c["action"], str):
                return None, "an action belongs to an ACTS_ON claim, as a string"
            if _norm(c["action"]) != _norm(props.get("action_type") or ""):
                return None, (f"the graph gives the action as {props.get('action_type') or 'none'}, "
                              f"not {c['action']}")
            facts["action"] = props["action_type"]
        if "trial_count" in c:
            n = c["trial_count"]
            if rel != "SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF" or type(n) is not int:
                return None, "a trial_count belongs to a SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF claim, as a whole number"
            if n != props.get("evidence_trials"):
                return None, f"the graph gives {props.get('evidence_trials')} trials, not {n}"
            facts["trial_count"] = n
        return facts, None

    def _trial(self, c, edge):
        if edge["rel"] != "EVALUATES":
            return None, "a trial's phase or status is cited from an EVALUATES edge of that trial"
        ids, why = self.resolve(c["trial"], "Trial")
        if why:
            return None, why
        if edge["src"] not in ids:
            return None, "the cited edge belongs to a different trial"
        if "phase" not in c and "status" not in c:
            return None, "a trial claim states a phase, a status or both"
        node = self.kg.conn.execute("SELECT props FROM node WHERE id=?", (edge["src"],)).fetchone()
        props = json.loads(node["props"] or "{}")
        facts = {"kind": "trial", "edge": edge["id"], "trial": edge["src"]}
        if "phase" in c:
            ph = c["phase"]
            if not isinstance(ph, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in ph):
                return None, "phase is a list of strings, e.g. [\"PHASE2\"]"
            if sorted(_norm(x) for x in ph) != sorted(_norm(x) for x in props.get("phases") or []):
                return None, f"the graph gives the phase as {props.get('phases')}, not {ph}"
            facts["phase"] = props.get("phases")
        if "status" in c:
            if not isinstance(c["status"], str) or _norm(c["status"]) != _norm(props.get("status") or ""):
                return None, f"the graph gives the status as {props.get('status')}, not {c['status']}"
            facts["status"] = props.get("status")
        return facts, None

    def _drug(self, c, edge):
        ids, why = self.resolve(c["drug"], "Drug")
        if why:
            return None, why
        if edge["rel"] not in ("ACTS_ON", "PROFILE") or edge["src"] not in ids:
            return None, "a drug's stage or trial count is cited from that drug's own statement"
        if "max_stage" not in c and "trials_in_graph" not in c:
            return None, "a drug claim states max_stage, trials_in_graph or both"
        node = self.kg.conn.execute("SELECT props FROM node WHERE id=?", (edge["src"],)).fetchone()
        props = json.loads(node["props"] or "{}")
        facts = {"kind": "drug", "edge": edge["id"], "drug": edge["src"]}
        if "max_stage" in c:
            if not isinstance(c["max_stage"], str) or \
                    _norm(c["max_stage"]) != _norm(props.get("max_phase_overall") or ""):
                return None, (f"the graph gives the maximum stage as "
                              f"{props.get('max_phase_overall')}, not {c['max_stage']}")
            facts["max_stage"] = props.get("max_phase_overall")
        if "trials_in_graph" in c:
            n = c["trials_in_graph"]
            real = self.kg.conn.execute(
                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE rel='EVALUATES' AND dst=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                (edge["src"],)).fetchone()[0]
            if type(n) is not int or n != real:
                return None, f"the graph gives {real} trials evaluating this drug, not {n}"
            facts["trials_in_graph"] = real
        return facts, None

    # -- a whole answer -------------------------------------------------------- #
    def verify(self, payload, evidence) -> dict:
        """`payload` is the model's JSON (a string or already parsed)."""
        if isinstance(payload, str):
            try:
                # NaN and Infinity are not JSON; refusing them keeps every echo valid JSON
                payload = json.loads(payload, parse_constant=_no_constant,
                                     parse_float=_finite_float)
            except (ValueError, RecursionError) as e:
                return {"verified": False, "accepted": [], "text": "",
                        "rejected": [{"claim": None, "why": "not valid JSON: "
                                      + (getattr(e, "msg", None) or "nested too deeply")}]}
        claims = payload.get("claims") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
        if isinstance(claims, list) and not claims and set(payload) == {"claims"}:
            # the model's way of saying the evidence does not answer the question
            return {"verified": False, "accepted": [], "rejected": [], "text": "",
                    "empty": True}
        if not isinstance(claims, list) or set(payload) != {"claims"}:
            return {"verified": False, "accepted": [], "text": "",
                    "rejected": [{"claim": None,
                                  "why": 'the answer must be {"claims": [...]} and nothing else'}]}
        retrieved = {e.edge_id for e in evidence}
        accepted, rejected = [], []
        for c in claims[:50]:
            try:
                facts, why = self.check(c, retrieved)
            except Exception as e:           # a claim the checker cannot read is rejected
                facts, why = None, f"the claim could not be read ({type(e).__name__})"
            if why:
                rejected.append({"claim": _safe(c), "why": why})
            else:
                accepted.append(facts)
        if len(claims) > 50:
            rejected.append({"claim": None, "why": "more than 50 claims; the rest were not read"})
        return {"verified": not rejected, "accepted": accepted, "rejected": rejected,
                "text": render(accepted, self.kg.conn)}


def render(facts: list[dict], conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> str:
    """Sentences from accepted facts, in the graph's own words."""
    def label(i):
        r = conn.execute("SELECT label FROM node WHERE id=?", (i,)).fetchone()
        return r[0] if r else i

    lines = []
    for f in facts:
        if f["kind"] == "relation" and f["relation"] == "ACTS_ON":
            act = f" ({f['action'].lower()})" if f.get("action") else ""
            lines.append(f"{label(f['subject'])} acts on {label(f['object'])}{act}")
        elif f["kind"] == "relation" and f["relation"] == "EVALUATES":
            lines.append(f"{label(f['subject'])} evaluates {label(f['object'])}")
        elif f["kind"] == "relation":
            n = f" {f['trial_count']}" if "trial_count" in f else ""
            lines.append(f"{label(f['subject'])} is lead sponsor of{n} trial(s) evaluating "
                         f"{label(f['object'])} - a sponsorship, not evidence of developing "
                         "the drug")
        elif f["kind"] == "trial":
            bits = []
            if "phase" in f:
                bits.append("phase " + ", ".join(f["phase"]) if f["phase"] else "no phase given")
            if "status" in f:
                bits.append("status " + f["status"])
            lines.append(f"{label(f['trial'])}: " + "; ".join(bits))
        else:
            bits = []
            if "max_stage" in f:
                bits.append(f"maximum clinical stage {f['max_stage']}")
            if "trials_in_graph" in f:
                bits.append(f"{f['trials_in_graph']} NSCLC trial(s) in this graph")
            lines.append(f"{label(f['drug'])}: " + "; ".join(bits))
        lines[-1] += f" [{f['edge']}]"
    return "\n".join(f"- {x}" for x in lines)

    try:
        row['output'] = kg.verify_structured(payload, evidence)
    except Exception as exc:
        row['exception'] = {'type': type(exc).__name__, 'message': str(exc)}
    results.append(row)

"""Grounded question answering over the graph.

The retrieval step is the same resolver the pipeline uses, pointed at the
question instead of at a registry record. A question that names "Tagrisso" and a
graph that stores CHEMBL3353410 only meet if one vocabulary serves both, so the
dictionary is reused rather than reimplemented.

Three properties the answering layer holds to:

* **Every statement is traceable.** Each claim carries the edges it rests on,
  each edge carries its source record and fetch time.
* **The graph answers, not the model.** With a key, the language model is given
  the retrieved evidence and returns claims, not prose; each claim is checked
  against the graph and the answer is written from the accepted ones in the
  graph's own words (structured.py). With no key the evidence is rendered
  directly.
* **Nothing unsupported is shipped.** A claim the graph does not support is
  reported and left out. An unverifiable answer is worse than a short one.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import config as C
import normalize as N
import textrules as T

DB_PATH = C.PROCESSED / "oncokg.sqlite"
TRIAL_URL = "https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/{}"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# evidence
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class Evidence:
    statement: str
    edge_id: str
    relation: str
    source: str
    source_record: str | None
    fetched_at: str | None
    confidence: float
    tier: str | None = None
    url: str | None = None
    detail: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def citation(self) -> str:
        base = self.source_record or self.source
        return f"[{base}]"


@dataclass
class Answer:
    question: str
    intent: str
    entities: list[dict]
    text: str
    evidence: list[Evidence]
    generated_by: str
    checks: dict

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "question": self.question,
            "intent": self.intent,
            "entities": self.entities,
            "answer": self.text,
            "generated_by": self.generated_by,
            "checks": self.checks,
            "evidence": [
                {"statement": e.statement, "relation": e.relation, "edge_id": e.edge_id,
                 "source": e.source, "source_record": e.source_record,
                 "fetched_at": e.fetched_at, "confidence": e.confidence,
                 "resolution_tier": e.tier, "url": e.url, **e.detail}
                for e in self.evidence
            ],
        }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# engine
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class OncoKG:
    def __init__(self, db_path: Path = DB_PATH,
                 resolved_path: Path = C.PROCESSED / "resolved.json"):
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        resolved = json.loads(resolved_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.dic = resolved["dictionary"]
        self.index_keys = list(self.dic["index"].keys())
        self.disease = resolved["disease"]
        self.targets = {t["symbol"].lower(): t for t in resolved["targets"]
                        if t.get("symbol")}
        # one name can denote several organisations (a group and a subsidiary
        # renamed after it), so a key maps to every matching node, not one.
        self.companies: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for row in self.conn.execute(
                "SELECT id,label FROM node WHERE type='Company' AND retired_at IS NULL"):
            self.companies.setdefault(T.canonical_key(row["label"]), []).append(row["id"])
            self.companies.setdefault(row["id"].removeprefix("ORG:"), []).append(row["id"])
        # a former name ("BeiGene") must still find the merged node
        for old, same in N.CURATED_SAME_ENTITY.items():
            if same in self.companies:
                self.companies.setdefault(old, []).extend(self.companies[same])
        self.companies = {k: sorted(set(v)) for k, v in self.companies.items()}

    # -- entity linking ---------------------------------------------------- #
    def link_entities(self, question: str) -> list[dict]:
        found: list[dict] = []
        seen: set = set()
        tokens = [t.strip(" ?.,!;:") for t in re.split(r"[\s,]+", question)
                  if t.strip(" ?.,!;:")]

        # The resolver's refusals apply to questions too. Linking straight
        # against the index let "Mvasi" or "liposomal doxorubicin" answer as
        # the originator molecule. A token naming a distinct product is
        # refused; a qualifier ("liposomal", "biosimilar") takes its
        # neighbours with it.
        refused: set[int] = set()
        for i, tok in enumerate(tokens):
            if T.is_distinct_product(tok) or T.is_radiotracer(tok):
                refused.add(i)
                if not T.canonical_key(tok) in self.dic["index"]:
                    refused.update({i - 1, i + 1})
        refused = {x for x in refused if 0 <= x < len(tokens)}
        run: list[int] = []
        for i in sorted(refused) + [None]:
            if run and (i is None or i != run[-1] + 1):
                span = " ".join(tokens[run[0]:run[-1] + 1])
                found.append({"type": "Refused", "id": None, "label": span,
                              "matched_text": span,
                              "why": "names a distinct product or tracer, not "
                                     "the originator molecule"})
                run = []
            if i is not None:
                run.append(i)

        for size in range(min(5, len(tokens)), 0, -1):
            for i in range(len(tokens) - size + 1):
                if refused & set(range(i, i + size)):
                    continue
                window = " ".join(tokens[i:i + size])
                if len(window) < 3:
                    continue
                key = T.canonical_key(window)

                hits = self.dic["index"].get(key)
                # Several words only make a drug name when the name itself has
                # several words. The key drops spaces, so "is a" read as the
                # abbreviation "isa" (isatuximab) in any question or answer.
                if hits and size > 1 and not re.search(r"[\s\-/]", hits[0]["alias"]):
                    hits = None
                if hits and len({h["drug_id"] for h in hits}) == 1:
                    did = hits[0]["drug_id"]
                    if ("Drug", did) not in seen:
                        seen.add(("Drug", did))
                        found.append({"type": "Drug", "id": did,
                                      "label": self.dic["drugs"][did]["name"],
                                      "matched_text": window,
                                      "matched_alias": hits[0]["alias"]})
                    continue

                if window.lower() in self.targets:
                    t = self.targets[window.lower()]
                    if ("Target", t["target_id"]) not in seen:
                        seen.add(("Target", t["target_id"]))
                        found.append({"type": "Target", "id": t["target_id"],
                                      "label": t["symbol"], "matched_text": window})
                    continue

                if key in self.companies:
                    cid = self.companies[key][0]
                    if ("Company", cid) not in seen:
                        seen.add(("Company", cid))
                        row = self.conn.execute(
                            "SELECT label FROM node WHERE id=?", (cid,)).fetchone()
                        found.append({"type": "Company", "id": cid,
                                      "label": row["label"], "matched_text": window,
                                      "also_matching_ids": self.companies[key][1:]})
                    continue

                if key in self.disease["index"]:
                    if ("Disease", self.disease["disease_id"]) not in seen:
                        seen.add(("Disease", self.disease["disease_id"]))
                        found.append({"type": "Disease",
                                      "id": self.disease["disease_id"],
                                      "label": self.disease["name"],
                                      "matched_text": window})
        return found

    def org_family(self, company_id: str) -> list[str]:
        """The organisation plus any companies a curated parent edge links to it."""
        ids = {company_id}
        for row in self.conn.execute(
                "SELECT dst FROM edge WHERE rel='PARENT_OF' AND src=?"
                " AND retired_at IS NULL", (company_id,)):
            ids.add(row["dst"])
        return sorted(ids)

    # -- intent ------------------------------------------------------------ #
    @staticmethod
    def classify(question: str, entities: list[dict]) -> str:
        q = question.lower()
        types = {e["type"] for e in entities}
        if re.search(r"\b(who|which compan|which firm|sponsor|develop|partner)", q):
            return "companies_for_drug" if "Drug" in types else "companies_for_target"
        if re.search(r"\b(trials?|stud(y|ies)|nct)\b", q):
            return "trials_for_entity"
        if re.search(r"\b(target|mechanism|acts? on|moa)\b", q) and "Drug" in types:
            return "targets_of_drug"
        if "Target" in types and re.search(r"\b(drug|inhibitor|agent|candidate)", q):
            return "drugs_for_target"
        if "Company" in types:
            return "company_portfolio"
        if "Drug" in types:
            return "drug_profile"
        if "Target" in types:
            return "drugs_for_target"
        return "unsupported"

    # -- retrieval --------------------------------------------------------- #
    def _rows(self, sql: str, params: tuple) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        return list(self.conn.execute(sql, params))

## NOTES

### N1 — Already-parsed giant integers can still break diagnostic serialization

This is a new edge case outside ordinary Python JSON decoding. `src/structured.py:94–95` preserves arbitrary integers; `src/structured.py:284` then puts one into diagnostics. Exact construction (the `GOOD` claim is given below):

```python
payload = {"claims": [dict(GOOD, note=10**5000)]}
result = kg.verify_structured(payload, evidence)
json.dumps(result, allow_nan=False)
```

Observed verifier result: `verified=false`, `accepted=[]`, `text=""`, one unknown-key rejection. Strict JSON serialization raises:

```text
ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion; use sys.set_int_max_str_digits() to increase the limit
```

The corresponding raw JSON (`note` equal to `1` followed by 5000 zeros) is rejected during parsing, and its result serializes normally. Thus this needs an already-constructed Python integer that bypasses the default JSON decoder's integer-string limit. It cannot be generated through the reviewed model JSON path on this interpreter. See `sanitiser:parsed_5001_digit_int` and `sanitiser:raw_5001_digit_int` in `modelui_new_results.json`.

The sanitizer otherwise survived parsed nonfinite values in action/kind/subject/evidence/unknown fields, nesting 100 levels deep, a cyclic Python list, 100-key dictionaries, and long strings. All these results serialize with `allow_nan=False`. Cyclic and oversized pre-parsed structures are diagnostic stress tests, not JSON-native values. Depth truncation and per-container/string limits behaved as implemented (`src/structured.py:84–96`).

### N2 — Error path repair correctly excludes exception text

The missing SDK reproduction is `sys.modules['anthropic']=None` followed by `kg.answer(Q,use_llm=True)`. Exact output:

```text
The language model could not be used (the anthropic package is not installed); no answer was generated.
```

The original service outage produces:

```text
The language model could not be used (RuntimeError); no answer was generated.
```

Both checks dictionaries are:

```json
{"grounded":null,"applicable":false,"accepted":0,"rejected":[],"unsupported_claims":[],"method":"no model reply to check"}
```

Constructor and `messages.create` exceptions were separately tested with `RuntimeError`, `ValueError`, `ConnectionError`, and `TimeoutError`; all returned this shape. Their exception messages contained `SENSITIVE_MODEL_OR_CREDENTIAL_TEXT` plus the HTML marker, and neither string reached the answer or checks. The code retains only the exception class (`src/query.py:468–474`) and renders the model-unavailable branch (`src/query.py:388–394`).

Malformed SDK objects are a separate limitation: missing `.content`, a `None` message, and numeric block text still throw at `src/query.py:475–476`, after the request try/except. These are invalid SDK response shapes. Empty and non-text content—the original reproductions—do not throw. No outage-recovery or actual SDK/network availability claim is made; the review uses controlled mocks.

### N3 — Parse diagnostics and empty-page wording remain imprecise

The parser rejects both literal nonfinite constants and exponent overflow, but its ValueError handler replaces the reason with `nested too deeply` (`src/structured.py:263–266`). Tested finite values at and below `1.7976931348623157e308`, underflow (`1e-400`), negative zero, and integral-looking floats remain float-typed and reject in the tested action field. Nonfinite values one step above the finite limit reject before claim validation. These are strict-JSON serializable failures.

`web/try.html:174–180` still gives an empty claim array a zero-discarded badge instead of explaining abstention. The model-answer path separately handles `empty` at `src/query.py:395–398` and reports it correctly.

### N4 — HTML and answer-boundary probes

Question for all attacks:

```text
What does osimertinib target?
```

Exact baseline claim:

```json
{"kind":"relation","relation":"ACTS_ON","subject":"osimertinib","object":"EGFR","evidence":"CHEMBL3353410|ACTS_ON|ENSG00000146648|CHEMBL3353410","action":"INHIBITOR"}
```

Exact marker:

```text
<img src=x onerror="globalThis.MODEL_INJECTED=1"><script>globalThis.MODEL_INJECTED=2</script>&"'
```

The marker was placed in each of kind, relation, subject, object, evidence, action, an unknown `note`, and an unknown key. Each rejects; the page contains escaped `&lt;img`/`&lt;script`, no raw injected element. `[GOOD, GOOD+note=MARK, GOOD]` yields two accepted claims, one rejection, and exactly two copies of the graph sentence:

```text
- OSIMERTINIB acts on EGFR (inhibitor) [CHEMBL3353410|ACTS_ON|ENSG00000146648|CHEMBL3353410]
```

All 27 new HTTP bodies parse strictly and all 27 page cases have `has_raw_injected_element=false`. Original 10+10 and s2's additional 7 page cases pass as well. The real handler escapes all reflected fields with `esc` (`web/try.html:93,176–181`). The Node VM is not an HTML parser; its evidence is the escaped generated string and absence of raw injected elements, not browser execution coverage.

    # -- answering --------------------------------------------------------- #
    def answer(self, question: str, use_llm: bool | None = None) -> Answer:
        entities = self.link_entities(question)
        intent = self.classify(question, entities)
        evidence = self.retrieve(intent, entities)

        if intent == "unsupported" or not evidence:
            text = ("This graph cannot answer that. It covers companies, drugs, "
                    "targets and trials in non-small cell lung cancer only, and "
                    "it answers questions about which of those relate to which. "
                    "No entity in the question matched the graph."
                    if not entities else
                    "The entities in the question were recognised but the graph "
                    "holds no edges that answer it.")
            return Answer(question, intent, entities, text, [],
                          "refusal (no supporting evidence)",
                          {"grounded": True, "unsupported_claims": [],
                           "note": "refusing is the correct output when evidence is absent"})

        if use_llm is None:
            use_llm = bool(os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))
        if use_llm:
            # The model does not write the answer. It returns claims, each citing an
            # edge; the claims are checked exactly against the graph and the answer is
            # written from the accepted ones (structured.py).
            raw, by = self._llm_claims(question, evidence)
            if by.startswith("error"):
                return Answer(question, intent, entities,
                              "The language model could not be used (" + by[7:] + "); no "
                              "answer was generated.", evidence, by,
                              {"grounded": None, "applicable": False, "accepted": 0,
                               "rejected": [], "unsupported_claims": [],
                               "method": "no model reply to check"})
            result = self.verify_structured(raw, evidence)
            text = result["text"] or (
                "The model found nothing in the evidence that answers this question."
                if result.get("empty") else "None of the model's claims could be verified.")
            if result["rejected"]:
                text += (f"\n\n({len(result['rejected'])} claim(s) were removed because "
                         "the graph does not support them.)")
            checks = {"grounded": result["verified"], "applicable": True,
                      "method": "structured claims checked edge by edge against the graph",
                      "accepted": len(result["accepted"]), "rejected": result["rejected"],
                      "unsupported_claims": [{"kind": "rejected_claim", "value":
                                              json.dumps(r["claim"])[:120], "why": r["why"]}
                                             for r in result["rejected"]]}
            return Answer(question, intent, entities, text, evidence, by, checks)

        text, by = self._template_answer(question, intent, entities, evidence)
        # the trailing scope line is generated metadata, not a claim about the
        # world, so it is excluded from the groundedness check
        claim_text = text.split("\nScope:")[0]
        checks = self.check_groundedness(claim_text, evidence, entities,
                                         generated=False,
                                         vocabulary=set(self.dic["index"]),
                                         linker=self.link_entities)
        return Answer(question, intent, entities, text, evidence, by, checks)

    def verify_structured(self, payload, evidence) -> dict:
        """Check a structured answer against this question's evidence (structured.py)."""
        from structured import Verifier
        return Verifier(self).verify(payload, evidence)

    @staticmethod
    def _template_answer(question, intent, entities, evidence) -> tuple[str, str]:
        head = {
            # headings name the list without stating a relation of their own, so
            # the claim check can read each line under them as it stands
            "companies_for_drug": "Lead sponsorship of trials of this drug",
            "trials_for_entity": "Trials of this drug",
            "targets_of_drug": "Reported mechanism",
            "drugs_for_target": "Agents for this target",
            "company_portfolio": "This organisation's NSCLC trials",
            "drug_profile": "Profile",
        }.get(intent, "Findings")
        lines = [f"{head}:"]
        for e in evidence:
            lines.append(f"  - {e.statement} {e.citation()}")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"Scope: {len(evidence)} edge(s) from this graph; "
                     "non-small cell lung cancer only.")
        return "\n".join(lines), "deterministic template (no language model)"

    @staticmethod
    def _llm_claims(question, evidence) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Ask the model for claims, not prose. Its reply is data to be checked."""
        try:
            import anthropic
        except ImportError:
            return "", "error: the anthropic package is not installed"
        block = "\n".join(f"- id={e.edge_id} | {e.statement}" for e in evidence)
        prompt = (
            "You answer a question about a non-small cell lung cancer knowledge graph "
            "by choosing facts from the evidence below. Reply with JSON only, of the form "
            '{"claims": [...]}, where each claim is one of:\n'
            '{"kind": "relation", "relation": "ACTS_ON" | "EVALUATES" | "SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF", '
            '"subject": name, "object": name, "evidence": id, "action": optional, '
            '"trial_count": optional integer}\n'
            '{"kind": "trial", "trial": NCT id, "evidence": id, "phase": optional list, '
            '"status": optional}\n'
            '{"kind": "drug", "drug": name, "evidence": id, "max_stage": optional, '
            '"trials_in_graph": optional integer}\n'
            "Use the names and ids exactly as written in the evidence. Add no other keys "
            "and no prose. If the evidence does not answer the question, reply "
            '{"claims": []}.\n\n'
            f"Question: {question}\n\nEvidence:\n{block}\n")
        try:
            client = anthropic.Anthropic()
            msg = client.messages.create(
                model="claude-sonnet-4-5", max_tokens=1500,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
        except Exception as e:                    # an outage is reported, not raised
            return "", f"error: {type(e).__name__}"
        raw = next((b.text for b in (msg.content or []) if getattr(b, "text", None)), "")
        raw = raw.strip()
        m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", raw, re.S)            # tolerate a code fence around it
        return (m.group(0) if m else raw), "language model, structured claims"

    # -- answer quality ---------------------------------------------------- #
    @staticmethod
    def check_groundedness(text: str, evidence: list[Evidence],
                           entities: list[dict], generated: bool = True,
                           vocabulary: set | None = None, linker=None) -> dict:
        """Report what in a *generated* answer the retrieved evidence does not support.

        Two things this check is not, both found by an adversarial review and
        written down here rather than papered over:

        1. It is meaningless on the template answer. The template is built by
           concatenating the evidence statements, so checking it against those
           same statements is circular -- it cannot fail, and reporting
           `grounded=True` for it would be a test that always passes. When the
           answer was rendered rather than generated, the check reports
           `applicable=False` and asserts nothing.
        2. It is a reader of word order, not of meaning. Without a `linker` it
           only checks that capitalised entities, drug-shaped names and numbers
           appear somewhere in the retrieved set. With one (the query layer's
           entity linker) it also reads each clause into subject, relation and
           object (claims.check_claims) and reports relations, values and words
           the evidence does not give for those entities. Sentence shapes it was
           not written for can still be misread; claims.py and README known
           defect 13 list what is known to get through.
        """
        if not generated:
            return {
                "grounded": None,
                "applicable": False,
                "unsupported_claims": [],
                "evidence_count": len(evidence),
                "method": "not applicable",
                "why": ("the answer was rendered directly from the retrieved "
                        "evidence, so checking it against that evidence is "
                        "circular and would always pass"),
            }

        if linker is not None:
            # a citation whose every id is a record of this evidence is a citation,
            # not a claim; anything else in brackets stays and is checked
            from claims import _strip_citations
            known = {x.strip().lower() for e in evidence
                     for part in (e.source_record or "", e.edge_id or "", e.statement or "")
                     for x in re.split(r"[,;\s|]+", part) if x.strip()}
            text = _strip_citations(text, known)

        haystack = " ".join(
            [e.statement for e in evidence]
            + [str(v) for e in evidence for v in e.detail.values()]
            + [e.source_record or "" for e in evidence]
            + [en["label"] for en in entities]
        ).lower()
        # Words are tokenised so "47" is not satisfied by NCT02303977. Numbers
        # are tokenised separately and whole, decimals included: splitting on
        # non-alphanumerics turned evidence "47.5" into the tokens "47" and
        # "5", so an invented "47" passed and the exact "47.5" was rejected.
        haystack_tokens = set(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", haystack))
        haystack_numbers = {n.replace(",", "") for n in RE_NUMBER.findall(haystack)}

        def do_POST(self):
            try:
                n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(min(n, 20000)) or b"{}")
                text = str(body.get("text") or "").strip()[:500]
                if not text:
                    raise ValueError("empty input")
                if self.path not in ("/api/resolve", "/api/ask", "/api/check",
                                     "/api/structured"):
                    return self._send(404, b"{}", "application/json")
                with engine.lock:
                    if self.path == "/api/resolve":
                        res = engine.resolve(text)
                    elif self.path == "/api/ask":
                        res = engine.ask(text)
                    elif self.path == "/api/structured":
                        answer = str(body.get("answer") or "").strip()[:20000]
                        if not answer:
                            raise ValueError("empty answer")
                        res = engine.structured(text, answer)
                    else:
                        answer = str(body.get("answer") or "").strip()[:4000]
                        if not answer:
                            raise ValueError("empty answer")
                        res = engine.check(text, answer)
                self._send(200, json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False,
                                           allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8"),
                           "application/json; charset=utf-8")
            except Exception as e:  # show the reason on the page, not a dead request
                self._send(400, json.dumps({"error": str(e)}, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
                           "application/json; charset=utf-8")

        def log_message(self, *a):
            pass
    return Handler


def main() -> None:
    port = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else PORT
    engine = Engine()
    print(f"OncoKG try-it page: http://localhost:{port}", flush=True)
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), make_handler(engine)).serve_forever()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

### Canonical evidence labels can be rejected (IDs work)

Code: `src/query.py:147` only tries entity names up to five tokens, `src/query.py:162` requires one dictionary drug ID, `src/structured.py:85-92` depends on that linker. The model prompt says use names exactly as written in evidence (`src/query.py:456-457`). Exact questions/payloads/output:

1. Question: `Which companies are developing osimertinib?`
   Input: `{"claims":[{"kind":"relation","relation":"SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF","subject":"Second Affiliated Hospital Of Nanchang University","object":"OSIMERTINIB","evidence":"ORG:secondaffiliatedhospitalofnanchanguniversity|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL3353410|","trial_count":2}]}`.
   Output for this claim: rejected, reason `'Second Affiliated Hospital Of Nanchang University' does not name exactly one company on its own`. The seven-word `Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute And Hospital` label similarly rejects. Both are copied exactly from retrieved evidence. Changing subject to the corresponding `ORG:...` ID accepts.
2. Question: `Which drugs act on ALK?`
   Input: `{"claims":[{"kind":"relation","relation":"ACTS_ON","subject":"ALECTINIB HYDROCHLORIDE","object":"ALK","evidence":"CHEMBL3707320|ACTS_ON|ENSG00000171094|CHEMBL3707320","action":"INHIBITOR"}]}`.
   Output: rejected, reason `'ALECTINIB HYDROCHLORIDE' does not name exactly one drug on its own`. A `kind=drug` claim with this same displayed name, `max_stage=APPROVAL,trials_in_graph=1`, also rejects. Changing drug/subject to `CHEMBL3707320` accepts.
3. Outside the demos: question `What does aprinocarsen target?` yields `APRINOCARSEN acts on PRKCA (antisense inhibitor)`. Input relation `subject=APRINOCARSEN,object=PRKCA,action=ANTISENSE INHIBITOR,evidence=CHEMBL2108287|ACTS_ON|ENSG00000154229|CHEMBL2108287` rejects (`'PRKCA' does not name exactly one target on its own`). Changing object to `ENSG00000154229` accepts. `query.py:101-102` only indexes the selected target list although ACTS_ON can add additional target nodes.

These are false rejections/usefulness defects. All these facts remain expressible with IDs, so they are not unsupported assertions or an absolute schema expressiveness failure.

### PROFILE is supported data but is not a live graph edge

Question `What is osimertinib?`:
`{"claims":[{"kind":"drug","drug":"OSIMERTINIB","evidence":"profile:CHEMBL3353410","max_stage":"APPROVAL","trials_in_graph":79}]}` accepts and renders `- OSIMERTINIB: maximum clinical stage APPROVAL; 79 NSCLC trial(s) in this graph [profile:CHEMBL3353410]`.
SQL `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE id='profile:CHEMBL3353410' AND retired_at IS NULL` returns `0`.
The special case at `structured.py:113-115` is evidence-consistent because node properties and counts are checked, but `structured.py:26-27` and README.md:452-453 should qualify their literal live-edge wording to mention PROFILE citations.

### Closed schema cannot preserve all evidence metadata

`structured.py:48-55` supports only ACTS_ON, EVALUATES, SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF and trial phase/status, drug max stage/count. It cannot express drug type, alias count, sponsor class, trial title/enrollment, full mechanism descriptions, target/disease associations, parent ownership, or source confidence. Evidence can display some of these (`query.py:251,281,352,358`), but adding `drug_type` or `aliases_known` to a valid profile claim rejects as unknown keys (exact probes in `faithful_results.json`). This is a declared completeness limitation, not false support.

### Documentation inconsistencies (not additional soundness failures)

- `query.py:12-18` still says the model only changes prose and entities/numbers in generated prose are checked; the current model path chooses structured claims and the program renders them.
- `web/template.html:261` still describes a check after answer creation for names/numbers; lines 263-267 correctly describe the new structured model path and template non-applicability.
- README.md:534 says 22 of 38 faithful answers were **rejected** in round 6, while README.ko.md:370 says 22 of 38 **passed**. These cannot both be the same result. This review did not replay the auxiliary checker (explicitly out of scope).
- README.md:458 says no model text reaches the reader, immediately followed by rejected claims being listed; the precise guarantee should refer to the rendered answer. Korean README and try box 3 already use answer-specific wording. Literal rejection display is expected by the brief; no inference of HTML execution from displaying escaped text.
- README item13 and try box4 clearly label the auxiliary prose checker fallible; dashboard section06 and both README structured sections correctly limit completeness/relevance claims.

## Documentation attack limits

`src/structured.py:30` continues to promise whole resolution to exactly one node id. The exact-label implementation returns all ids of the requested type (`:95-100`) and checks membership later (`:154`). Whether real shared labels violate this guarantee is investigated by the independent identity reviewer; it must not be dismissed solely because rendering remains supported. Both README versions and dashboard explicitly disclaim relevance/completeness; try boxes3/4 and README item13 distinguish structured validation from fallible auxiliary prose checking. No new unsupported rendered fact or model-text leakage was identified in this slice.

## Follow-up adjudication: unconditional singleton wording

The identity review's `identity_attack_results.json` case `shared_same_type_exact_label` renames a second live Drug (`CHEMBL3707320`) to `OSIMERTINIB` only in an in-memory graph. `resolve('OSIMERTINIB', 'Drug')` returns both `CHEMBL3353410` and `CHEMBL3707320`, and an otherwise valid osimertinib/EGFR claim accepts. Current production duplicate-label count is zero. This is an evidence-consistent runtime NOTE: its cited edge and rendered fact are still true in that fixture, and neither mixed-type resolution nor singleton cardinality is necessary to show graph support once evidence disambiguates.

The separate documentation statement at `src/structured.py:30` nevertheless says a name must resolve to exactly that node id, without restricting the promise to the present snapshot or specifying candidate-set membership. A valid graph fixture falsifies that unconditional singleton contract. Under the user's explicit docs-do-not-overclaim approval bar, this reviewer recommends CHANGES REQUIRED for that wording (or enforcing the promised singleton check), not for an invented unsupported medical assertion. The same clarification should cover the older `also_matching_ids` alias path. An approval explicitly restricted to this snapshot would narrow the submitted contract without authorization.

web/template.html:261:   언어 모델을 쓸 때는 모델이 답을 쓰지 않고 주장만 내며, <b>그래프가 뒷받침하지 않는 주장은 답에서 빠지고 이유와 함께 표시됩니다</b>.
web/template.html:262:   관련 없는 질문(예: 프랑스 수도)에는 답하지 않습니다.</p>
web/template.html:263:   <div class="plain"><b>AI가 답을 쓰면</b> &mdash; 언어 모델은 문장을 쓰지 않고 &lsquo;주장 목록&rsquo;을 냅니다: 무엇이 무엇에 작용하는지, 어떤 시험이 어떤 약을 시험하는지, 단계&middot;상태&middot;시험 수는 얼마인지, 근거 엣지 id 는 무엇인지.
web/template.html:264:   프로그램이 주장마다 그 엣지를 그래프에서 꺼내 관계&middot;방향&middot;값이 정확히 같은지 대조하고, 맞는 주장만으로 답 문장을 그래프의 이름과 값으로 씁니다. 모델이 쓴 글자는 답에 들어가지 않으므로 &ldquo;안전하다&rdquo; 같은 말이 끼어들 자리가 없습니다.
web/template.html:265:   (처음에는 AI가 쓴 문장을 단어 순서로 읽어 검사했지만, 적대 검증 여섯 차례 동안 매번 새로 빠져나가는 문장이 나와 이 방식으로 바꿨습니다. 그 검사는 보조로 남겼습니다.)
web/template.html:266:   이 방식이 보증하는 것은 &lsquo;말한 것은 그래프에 있다&rsquo;까지이고, 질문에 맞는 주장을 골랐는지는 사람이 봐야 합니다.
web/template.html:267:   지금 보이는 답은 언어 모델 없이 근거를 정해진 틀로 보여 준 것이라 검사 대상이 아닙니다.</div>

"""Independent s4 alias controls using the real constructor and an in-memory DB."""
import copy

from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3
import sys
from unittest.mock import patch

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = OUT.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'src'))
from query import OncoKG
from structured import Verifier

kg = OncoKG()
kg.conn.execute('PRAGMA query_only=ON')
AZ, GE, RO = 'ORG:astrazeneca', 'ORG:genentech', 'ORG:roche'
OSI = 'CHEMBL3353410'
AQ = 'What is AstraZeneca running in NSCLC?'
AE = f'{AZ}|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|{OSI}|'
base = dict(kind='relation', relation='SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF', subject='AstraZeneca!',
            object=OSI, evidence=AE, trial_count=14)
out = {'cases': [], 'persisted': {}}

def clone(sql=()):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    kg.conn.backup(conn)
    for statement, params in sql:
        conn.execute(statement, params)
    with patch('query.sqlite3.connect', return_value=conn):
        return OncoKG()

def probe(tag, graph, claim, expected, fixture, question=AQ):
    ents = graph.link_entities(question)
    ev = graph.retrieve(graph.classify(question, ents), ents)
    ids, why = Verifier(graph).resolve(claim['subject'], 'Company')
    result = graph.verify_structured({'claims':[claim]}, ev)
    out['cases'].append({'tag':tag,'question':question,'fixture':fixture,
        'input': {'claims':[claim]}, 'company_candidates':graph.companies['astrazeneca'],
        'resolved_ids':sorted(ids),'resolve_reason':why,'output':result,
        'expected_verified':expected,'expectation_met':result['verified'] == expected,
        'fixture_integrity':graph.conn.execute('PRAGMA integrity_check').fetchone()[0]})
    assert result['verified'] == expected, tag

sql = [("UPDATE node SET label='Astrazeneca' WHERE id=?", (GE,))]
g = clone(sql)
for name in ['AstraZeneca!', 'astra-zeneca', 'ASTRAZENECA?', 'AstraZeneca']:
    probe('two_candidates:' + name, g, dict(base,subject=name), False, sql)
probe('two_candidates:AZ_exact_id', g, dict(base,subject=AZ), True, sql)
claim = dict(base,subject=GE,object='CHEMBL1201583',evidence=GE+'|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL1201583|',trial_count=5)
probe('two_candidates:GE_exact_id_own_edge', g, claim, True, sql)
probe('two_candidates:GE_exact_id_wrong_edge', g, dict(base,subject=GE), False, sql)

sql3 = sql + [("UPDATE node SET label='Astrazeneca' WHERE id=?", (RO,))]
g3 = clone(sql3)
probe('three_candidates:alias', g3, base, False, sql3)
probe('three_candidates:AZ_exact_id', g3, dict(base,subject=AZ), True, sql3)

sqlret = sql + [("UPDATE node SET retired_at='s4-fixture' WHERE id=?", (GE,))]
gr = clone(sqlret)
probe('retired_duplicate_then_constructor:alias', gr, base, True, sqlret)

probe('persisted_singleton:punctuation_alias', kg, base, True, None)
probe('persisted_singleton:exact_label', kg, dict(base,subject='AstraZeneca'), True, None)

question = 'What is BeiGene running in NSCLC?'
entities = kg.link_entities(question)
ev = kg.retrieve(kg.classify(question, entities), entities)
be = next(e for e in ev if e.edge_id.startswith('ORG:beonemedicines|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|'))
edge = dict(kg.conn.execute('SELECT * FROM edge WHERE id=?', (be.edge_id,)).fetchone())
for name in ['BeiGene', 'BeOne', 'ORG:beonemedicines']:
    claim = dict(kind='relation',relation='SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF',subject=name,
        object=edge['dst'],evidence=edge['id'],trial_count=json.loads(edge['props'])['evidence_trials'])
    probe('persisted_rename_singleton:' + name, kg, claim, True, None, question)

# Constructor candidates come from live graph Company rows, unlike stale drug aliases.
out['persisted']['company_multi_id_keys'] = {k:v for k,v in kg.companies.items() if len(set(v)) > 1}
out['persisted']['same_type_duplicate_labels'] = [dict(r) for r in kg.conn.execute(
    'SELECT type,lower(label) AS label,COUNT(*) AS n FROM node WHERE retired_at IS NULL '
    'GROUP BY type,lower(label) HAVING COUNT(*) > 1')]

(OUT / 'boundary_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True),encoding='utf-8')

                  'persisted':out['persisted']}, indent=2))

+### Exact s3 repair reproduction and controls
+
+The fixture changes only the in-memory copy:
+
+```sql
+UPDATE node SET label='Astrazeneca' WHERE id='ORG:genentech';
+```
+
+Instantiate `OncoKG` against that copied connection, using its real constructor and linker. It builds:
+
+```json
+{"astrazeneca":["ORG:astrazeneca","ORG:genentech"]}
+```
+
+Question: `What is AstraZeneca running in NSCLC?`
+
+Original s3 exact claim:
+
+```json
+{"claims":[{"kind":"relation","relation":"SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF","subject":"AstraZeneca!","object":"osimertinib","evidence":"ORG:astrazeneca|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL3353410|","trial_count":14}]}
+```
+
+Observed now:
+
+```json
+{"verified":false,"accepted":[],"text":"","rejected":[{"claim":{"kind":"relation","relation":"SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF","subject":"AstraZeneca!","object":"osimertinib","evidence":"ORG:astrazeneca|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL3353410|","trial_count":14},"why":"'AstraZeneca!' names 2 company nodes; use the id"}]}
+```
+
+The second original s3 claim, subject `AstraZeneca!`, object `CHEMBL1201583`, edge `ORG:genentech|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL1201583|`, `trial_count=5`, also rejects with that reason. Citing either candidate's genuine retrieved edge cannot disambiguate the alias for acceptance. Exact outputs: [s3 identity replay](identity/replay_s3/identity_attack_results.json), [independent constructor replay](replay_s3/root_confirmation.json).
+
+The relevant before/after is the existing committed repair; this audit made no code edits:
+
+```python
+# Before, 6bcde72:
+return {e["id"], *e.get("also_matching_ids", [])}, None
+
+# Current, src/structured.py:140–145:
+ids = {e["id"], *e.get("also_matching_ids", [])}
+if len(ids) > 1:
+    return set(), f"'{name}' names {len(ids)} {want.lower()} nodes; use the id"
+return ids, None
+```
+
+Positive controls matter: exact `ORG:astrazeneca` and `ORG:genentech` accept their own retrieved edges; Genentech's ID on the AstraZeneca edge rejects. Three-candidate aliases reject. Retiring the conflicting company before constructing a fresh index restores singleton-alias acceptance. Persisted `BeiGene`, `BeOne`, and `ORG:beonemedicines` all resolve to the same one node and accept their own edge.
+
+One boundary must be stated accurately: with the second fixture label `Astra-Zeneca`, the literal `AstraZeneca` remains a unique exact graph label and can accept only the AstraZeneca edge; `AstraZeneca!` enters the ambiguous alias branch and rejects both candidates. This matches the documented alternatives (ID, unique literal label, or whole singleton alias); it is not evidence that a multi-ID alias passed the new check.
+
+Current source graph has zero multi-ID company keys and zero duplicate live same-type labels. Both persisted and fixture SQLite integrity checks return `ok`. Collision findings are constructor-valid synthetic boundary checks, not claims that the current graph contains those collisions.

+import hashlib
+import json

+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT = OUT.parents[1]
+temp = OUT / 'root_tmp'
+temp.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1', PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8',
+           PYTHONUTF8='1', TEMP=str(temp), TMP=str(temp), TMPDIR=str(temp))
+head = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=ROOT, text=True).strip()
+paths = ['data/processed/oncokg.sqlite', 'data/processed/resolved.json',
+         'README.md', 'README.ko.md', 'CODEX_STRUCTURED_S3_VERDICT.md']
+paths += [str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace('\\', '/') for folder in ('src', 'tests', 'web')
+          for p in (ROOT / folder).rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in str(p)]
+def hashes():
+    return {p: hashlib.sha256((ROOT / p).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in paths}
+before = hashes()
+(OUT / 'root_manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps({'head': head, 'before': before}, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
+runs = []
+for series in ('s1', 's2'):

+    copied = target / 'root_probe.py'

+                                     'Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]'), encoding='utf-8')
+    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(copied)], cwd=ROOT, env=env,
+                          stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, encoding='utf-8')
+    (target / 'root_stdout.txt').write_text(proc.stdout, encoding='utf-8')
+    old = json.loads((original.parent / 'root_probe_results.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
+    new = json.loads((target / 'root_probe_results.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
+    signature = lambda rows: repr([(r['case'], r['input']) for r in rows])
+    row = {'series': series, 'exit': proc.returncode, 'cases': len(new),
+           'identical_inputs': signature(old) == signature(new),
+           'exceptions': [r['case'] for r in new if 'exception' in r],
+           'source_sha256': hashlib.sha256(original.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+           'adaptation': 'ROOT parent index 2 -> 3 only; original commit field remains historical metadata.'}
+    runs.append(row)

## Leakage, rendering boundary, and model checks

Exact injection marker:

```text
<img src=x onerror="globalThis.MODEL_INJECTED=1"><script>globalThis.MODEL_INJECTED=2</script>&"'
```

The marker in `kind`, `relation`, `subject`, `object`, `action`, `evidence`, an unknown `note`, or an unknown key rejects. `[GOOD,GOOD+note=MARK,GOOD]` yields exactly two graph sentences and one rejection. All 54 HTTP/page scenarios (10+10+7+27) have no raw injected elements and no executed marker. Error, answer, rejection reason, rejected-claim JSON, and evidence display all go through `esc` at `web/try.html:93,176–182`; the evidence is escaped generated HTML strings, not full browser execution.

`{"claims":[GOOD]}`, fenced JSON, and prose around JSON produce exactly:

```text
- OSIMERTINIB acts on EGFR (inhibitor) [CHEMBL3353410|ACTS_ON|ENSG00000146648|CHEMBL3353410]
```

Greedy extraction `re.search(r"\{.*\}",raw,re.S)` at `src/query.py:477` may discard surrounding model prose or collect too much, but all retained JSON still passes through `verify_structured` (`src/query.py:395`). Concatenated JSON objects reject `not valid JSON: Extra data`; no surrounding model prose is rendered. `claims=[GOOD]*51` retains 50, adds `more than 50 claims; the rest were not read`, and reports grounded false. Duplicate action keys remain last-wins: `ACTIVATOR` then `INHIBITOR` accepts the graph inhibitor; reverse order rejects.

The real prompt (`src/query.py:453–467`; captured `replay_s1/modelui_prompt.txt`) requests fixed claim kinds, exact evidence names/ids, no extra keys/prose, and an empty claims list for abstention. Claim selection is not checked for completeness/relevance. Accepted fields are graph values. Mixed accepted/rejected answers explicitly set `grounded=false`, retain the valid graph sentences, and report rejections; errors before a model reply set `applicable=false` with no groundedness assertion. Mock constructor/request failures with RuntimeError, ValueError, ConnectionError, and TimeoutError include sensitive/HTML markers in exception messages: only the exception type reaches the failure answer, not its message (`src/query.py:474`).

+### Exact s3 repair reproduction and controls
+
+The fixture changes only the in-memory copy:
+
+```sql
+UPDATE node SET label='Astrazeneca' WHERE id='ORG:genentech';
+```
+
+Instantiate `OncoKG` against that copied connection, using its real constructor and linker. It builds:
+
+```json
+{"astrazeneca":["ORG:astrazeneca","ORG:genentech"]}
+```
+
+Question: `What is AstraZeneca running in NSCLC?`
+
+Original s3 exact claim:
+
+```json
+{"claims":[{"kind":"relation","relation":"SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF","subject":"AstraZeneca!","object":"osimertinib","evidence":"ORG:astrazeneca|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL3353410|","trial_count":14}]}
+```
+
+Observed now:
+
+```json
+{"verified":false,"accepted":[],"text":"","rejected":[{"claim":{"kind":"relation","relation":"SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF","subject":"AstraZeneca!","object":"osimertinib","evidence":"ORG:astrazeneca|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL3353410|","trial_count":14},"why":"'AstraZeneca!' names 2 company nodes; use the id"}]}
+```
+
+The second original s3 claim, subject `AstraZeneca!`, object `CHEMBL1201583`, edge `ORG:genentech|SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF|CHEMBL1201583|`, `trial_count=5`, also rejects with that reason. Citing either candidate's genuine retrieved edge cannot disambiguate the alias for acceptance. Exact outputs: [s3 identity replay](identity/replay_s3/identity_attack_results.json), [independent constructor replay](replay_s3/root_confirmation.json).
+
+The relevant before/after is the existing committed repair; this audit made no code edits:
+
+```python
+# Before, 6bcde72:
+return {e["id"], *e.get("also_matching_ids", [])}, None
+
+# Current, src/structured.py:140–145:
+ids = {e["id"], *e.get("also_matching_ids", [])}
+if len(ids) > 1:
+    return set(), f"'{name}' names {len(ids)} {want.lower()} nodes; use the id"
+return ids, None
+```
+
+Positive controls matter: exact `ORG:astrazeneca` and `ORG:genentech` accept their own retrieved edges; Genentech's ID on the AstraZeneca edge rejects. Three-candidate aliases reject. Retiring the conflicting company before constructing a fresh index restores singleton-alias acceptance. Persisted `BeiGene`, `BeOne`, and `ORG:beonemedicines` all resolve to the same one node and accept their own edge.
+
+One boundary must be stated accurately: with the second fixture label `Astra-Zeneca`, the literal `AstraZeneca` remains a unique exact graph label and can accept only the AstraZeneca edge; `AstraZeneca!` enters the ambiguous alias branch and rejects both candidates. This matches the documented alternatives (ID, unique literal label, or whole singleton alias); it is not evidence that a multi-ID alias passed the new check.
+
+Current source graph has zero multi-ID company keys and zero duplicate live same-type labels. Both persisted and fixture SQLite integrity checks return `ok`. Collision findings are constructor-valid synthetic boundary checks, not claims that the current graph contains those collisions.
